turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you to the clinic?
turns.patient_response:
Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Well, I suppose I'm here because... I just feel like I’m always up and moving. Which is a good thing at my age, right? It's good to stay active. But, um, I guess it's just that even on a quiet day, I'm sort of bouncing around. Like, I'll start looking at the garden club list, and then... I'll wander over to my knitting bag, and then suddenly I'm looking at some travel papers. And I do all that before I’ve really finished any one thing. 

It's nothing terrible, really! Just a little scattered sometimes. Is that the sort of thing you wanted to know? I want to make sure I'm explaining it right for you.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient describes starting multiple activities (garden club list, knitting, travel papers) and moving on before finishing any of them, indicating difficulty sustaining attention.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient explicitly states feeling like they are 'always up and moving' and 'bouncing around' even on quiet days.

turns.doctor_question: Has this tendency to jump from one task to another been present for most of your life, or did it start more recently?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, goodness... well, if I'm being completely honest, I think it's been this way for most of my life. Even way back in grade school, I remember my teachers telling my mother that I was a very bright girl—which was always so nice of them to say! But, um, they did mention I was a little scattered, too. 

I guess I had a habit of misplacing my school papers, and maybe talking out of turn sometimes when I just got a little too excited to share something. And... well, I was always wiggling around in my seat before I actually finished my assignments. Just full of beans, my mother used to say! Nothing bad, of course. Just... a very energetic little girl who had a hard time sitting still. 

Is that the kind of history you were looking for? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient confirms the doctor's premise of jumping from task to task, noting she has been 'scattered' for most of her life.
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient mentions moving around before she had actually finished her school assignments.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient recalls having a habit of misplacing her school papers.
symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient explicitly describes 'wiggling around in my seat' and having a hard time sitting still.
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient admits to 'talking out of turn' in class when she was too excited to share something.
